about: What the command line, setup --print, doctor, ping and the server print, in English. {name} and {command} come from product.json; the other {placeholders} are filled where the text is used. A list is printed one line per item.
help: {name} {version}: local agent-behaviour analytics, one process + one small database.
A page script on your site (rrweb replay + clicks/typing + environment signals) sends visits to {name}'s own
collect endpoint; {name} stores them in SQLite on this computer, and its model judges, action by action,
whether a human or an AI agent was acting, which agent it was, and the human/agent share of each session.
After install you open a local page (http://127.0.0.1:{port}/): register, then it shows how to connect your
website (one line in its pages; for a public website, {name} on a server it can reach). Python {python} or newer,
standard library only.
Install dir:  $CAKE_HOME (default ~/.cake): config.json, cake.db (SQLite), replays/ (compressed replay chunks),
cake.pid, cake.log. `{command} migrate` copies a 0.3.4 database's replays into chunks (after a backup).
Port:         $CAKE_PORT or config "port" (default {port}). The local page listens on 127.0.0.1 only, always.
Settings:     {command} config get lists every setting, its value and where it comes from (default, user, env).
Server mode, for a public website's visitors: the same {name} on a small server your website can reach, behind
your site's load balancer, at a path of your own site (e.g. https://example.com/cake/). It adds a
SECOND listener, `public_listen` (e.g. 0.0.0.0:8080), that answers ONLY the page script, the rrweb recorder, the
collect endpoint and a health check, under `path_prefix` (e.g. /cake). The local page (dashboard, replay,
settings) stays on 127.0.0.1: open it through an SSH tunnel. With `trust_lb` on, the visitor's address, country,
TLS fingerprint and protocol are read from headers the load balancer sets ({lb_headers}); the address is used to
look up published ranges (agentcake/data/lists/) and is never stored. A site's server can hand {name} what only
it saw about the page request as a signed token (Server-Timing `cake`, shared secret in $CAKE_HOME/srv_secret,
`{command} secret init`); cake.js forwards it, {name} checks it.
Keeping data: every session is recorded and kept; nothing is deleted by age unless you choose 30 or 90 days.
The database has a disk budget (`budget_mb`, default {budget_mb}). From {warn_pct}% the dashboard and settings warn,
with how long until full at last week's pace. When it is full and `auto_free` is on (default), {name}
removes the REPLAYS (rrweb events) of the oldest human-only sessions, keeping their verdict, shares, timeline and
server half; a session an agent took part in is never removed to keep the budget. When the disk itself has less
than `disk_min_free_mb` free (default {disk_min_free_mb} MB), {name} keeps storing new replays and removes the
oldest ones instead, human-only sessions first, then those of any session without activity for `auto_free_quiet_ms`,
keeping everything else of them; when removing all of those would still leave less free (other files fill the
disk), it removes none. Then, or with `auto_free` off, {name} stops storing new replay events until there is room
again but still records each visit and its verdict.
Commands: start | stop | status | serve (foreground, for systemd) | setup --print | setup --print --site [--dir DIR]
config get [key] | config set <key> <value> | snippet | doctor [--dir DIR] [--url URL] | ping | sentence
--version
secret init | secret print (the server-half secret, for the site's server; printed only when asked)
lists (age and sources of the bundled name and IP lists) | lists update (the only command that goes online)
migrate [--dry-run] (0.3.4 replays into compressed chunks; backs the database up first)
logs import <file>... [--since 10m] [--to URL] (page requests from an nginx, Apache or Caddy access log)
logs formats (the log formats it reads, and the recommended lines for each web server)
delete --session <id> | --visitor <visit id> [--dry-run] (every trace of a visit: database, replays,
backups/, cake.log; works while {name} runs)
eval [--gate] [--out DIR] (how well it judges sessions with known answers, GOAL's thresholds)
lists_not_updated: lists not updated, the ones in use stay: {error}

eval_options.about: How well {name} judges sessions with known answers (our lab, clean human recordings, splices, a CAKE_HOME's labelled sessions, PostHog replays as reference), and GOAL's thresholds. Reads only.
eval_options.gate: exit 0 only when every threshold this command measures passes (1 when one fails or has no data)
eval_options.out: folder to write eval.md and eval.json into
eval_options.no_logistic: skip training the lab's logistic regression on its splices (it takes minutes)
eval_options.sources: JSON file naming this computer's data folders (default: eval/sources.json of a checkout)
eval_options.recordings: the S1.5 recorder's data folder (sessions/<run>.ndjson, logs/server.jsonl)
eval_options.cake_home: the CAKE_HOME whose sessions eval/truth_goal.jsonl lists (default: the current one)
eval_options.truth_goal: the list of labelled CAKE_HOME sessions (default: eval/truth_goal.jsonl)
eval_options.truth_manual: the list of clean human recordings
eval_options.truth_recordings: the list of agent and hand-off recordings
eval_options.thresholds: the thresholds file (default: eval/thresholds.json of a checkout)
eval_options.selfcollect: the data folder of the recorder copy our own runs used (Claude Code with an MCP server, automation dressed up as a human)
eval_options.truth_selfcollect: the list of our own runs' recordings

eval_no_thresholds: No thresholds file: {command} eval reads eval/thresholds.json and its data sets from a checkout of {name}'s source, which a release does not carry. Run the checkout's bin/{command} eval, or give --thresholds and the data sets (see {command} eval --help).
eval_gate_pass: Gate: every threshold measured here passes.
eval_gate_fail: Gate: not passing (failed or no data): {ids}.
logs_imported: {file} ({format}): {lines} lines; {sent} page requests sent: {matched} matched a visit, {duplicates} were already imported, {unmatched} matched no visit and were dropped; {skipped} other lines skipped, {older} older than --since, {unreadable} unreadable.
logs_missing: Not in this log format: {fields}. `{command} logs formats` prints the recommended format for nginx, Apache and Caddy.
logs_empty: Empty on every page request of this log: {fields}. Something in front of the web server (a proxy or a CDN) may remove them.
logs_no_format: {file}: no line of it is in a format {name} knows; give yours with --nginx-format or --apache-format.
logs_format_lacks: the log format has no {fields}; {name} needs each line's time, address, request, status and User-Agent
logs_bad_since: --since takes a number and a unit, s, m, h or d: for example --since 10m
logs_no_secret: no server-half secret in {path}: on the {name} server `{command} secret print` prints it; put it there through a pipe (SERVER.md, "Server logs")
logs_refused_secret: {url} answered {status}: the server-half secret in {path} is not the one of that {name}
logs_refused: {url} answered {status}: the records were not taken
logs_unreachable: nothing answers at {url}: is {name} running there? ({error})
delete_usage: usage: {command} delete --session <id> | --visitor <visit id> (each as often as needed) [--dry-run]
delete_bad_id: not a session id: "{id}" ({name}'s ids are letters and digits, at most {max} of them); nothing was deleted
delete_unsure_running: {pid_file} names process {pid}, which is running, but no {name} answers on port {port}, so nothing was deleted. If {name} runs on another port, run this again with CAKE_PORT set to it; if process {pid} is not {name}, delete {pid_file}.
delete_done: deleted {id}: {rows} rows, and {chunks} replay chunks ({bytes:,} bytes) overwritten with zeros
delete_would: would delete {id}: {rows} rows and {chunks} replay chunks ({bytes:,} bytes)
delete_backups: deleted {rows} rows from {files} backup(s) in backups/
delete_backups_would: would delete {rows} rows from {files} backup(s) in backups/
delete_log_would: would remove {lines} lines naming it from {log}
delete_reclaim: replay space given back: {deleted} chunk files deleted, {compacted} compacted, {bytes:,} bytes
delete_not_rewritten: {file} could not be rewritten ({error}): what was deleted may leave traces in its free space until it is. Free some disk space and run the same command again.
delete_wal_busy: a reader still had the write-ahead log of {file} open, so it still holds old pages; run the same command again to empty it.
delete_api_bad_body: Send {{"sessions": ["<session id>", ...]}} (ids of letters and digits), or {{"all": true}} for every session.
secret_created: secret created: {path} (mode 600, not printed). Give the same value to your site's server with: {command} secret print

invalid_setting.path_prefix: path_prefix: letters, digits, dots, dashes and slashes only, e.g. /cake
invalid_setting.public_listen: public_listen: host:port, e.g. 0.0.0.0:8080 (empty turns server mode off)
invalid_setting.site_key: site_key: ck_ followed by 3-40 letters, digits or _
invalid_setting.mask_inputs: mask_inputs: no longer a setting; the page script always masks what visitors type (agentcake/data/privacy.json)

python_too_old: {name} needs Python {python} or newer, and this is Python {version} ({executable}). Install a newer Python 3 (3.14 or newer also keeps replays smaller) and run {command} with it.
did_not_stop: {name} (pid {pid}) was asked to stop but has not exited after {seconds} s; see {log}. Run  {launcher} stop  again to wait longer.
stop_not_allowed: {name} (pid {pid}) could not be stopped from here: {error}. It may run as another user, or a sandbox (an AI tool's) may not allow it; run  {launcher} stop  in your own terminal.
stop_pid_unreadable: {name} was not stopped: {file} holds no process id: {error}
public_listening: {name} public listener on {listen} prefix={prefix} trust_lb={trust_lb} server half={half} ranges={ranges}
ping_sent: Self-check visit sent (page script HTTP {status}); it is marked as a test.
ping_failed: Could not send the self-check visit: {error}
doctor_replays_zlib: (Python {version} has no compression.zstd, so replays are stored with zlib and take more disk; Python 3.14+ uses zstd)
doctor_replays_unreadable: {count} stored chunks are zstd and need Python 3.14+ to be read
doctor_replays_blocked: not checked: writing in {folder} is not allowed from here ({error}), though its permissions allow it: most likely a sandbox (an AI tool's) blocks writing outside its own folder, not a problem with {name}'s storage. Ask the user to run  {launcher} doctor  in their own terminal to check it
doctor_site_none: Your own website (optional): not connected. Fine; connect it only if the user asks (setup --print --site).
doctor_site_script: page script found in website files
doctor_logs_info: {format}, last import {when}: {records} page requests, {matched} matched a visit
doctor_logs_no_address: ; no line can match: the uploads carry no visitor address (turn on trust_lb behind your load balancer, SERVER.md)
doctor_logs_formats: (`{command} logs formats` prints the recommended format)
doctor_sandbox_note: Note: if '{command} start' fails with 'Operation not permitted', a sandbox is blocking local network access, not {name}.
doctor_blocked: no connection to {base} is allowed from here ({error}): a sandbox (an AI tool's) blocks local network access, so this cannot tell whether {name} runs; it may well be running
doctor_blocked_next: {name} itself may be fine. Do not start it again: ask the user to run  {launcher} doctor  in their own terminal, or to give this tool network access (Codex: -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true).
doctor_not_checked_blocked: not checked: the sandbox blocks connections to 127.0.0.1
doctor_not_health: something answers on {base}, but not {name}'s health check (HTTP {status})
doctor_all_passed_warn: All checks passed, with {count} warning(s) above. Open {base}/
doctor_python_no_zstd: compression.zstd: no (replays are stored with zlib and take about 1.4 times the disk; Python 3.14+ has zstd)
doctor_disk_ok: {free} MB free on the disk of {folder}; below {floor} MB (disk_min_free_mb) {below}
doctor_disk_frees: the oldest replays are deleted to make room, human-only sessions first, and new replays are still stored
doctor_disk_off_info: {free} MB free on the disk of {folder}; {off}
doctor_disk_replays_stop: new replays will not be stored (visits and verdicts still are)
doctor_disk_low: only {free} MB free on the disk of {folder}, below disk_min_free_mb ({floor} MB), {why}: {replays_stop}. {fix}
doctor_disk_freeing: only {free} MB free on the disk of {folder}, below disk_min_free_mb ({floor} MB): {frees}. To keep the old replays, free some space or lower the floor:  {launcher} config set disk_min_free_mb <MB>
doctor_disk_full_other: only {free} MB free on the disk of {folder}, below disk_min_free_mb ({floor} MB), {other_files}. Until there is room, {replays_stop}; {resume}. {fix}
doctor_disk_other_files: and other files fill it: deleting every old replay would still leave less than {floor} MB free, so {name} deleted none
doctor_disk_replays_resume: they start again on their own
doctor_disk_fix: Free some space, or lower the floor:  {launcher} config set disk_min_free_mb <MB>
doctor_disk_fix_auto_free: Free some space, lower the floor:  {launcher} config set disk_min_free_mb <MB>  or let {name} delete the oldest replays:  {launcher} config set auto_free on
doctor_lists_info: built {built}, {age} day(s) old ({location}; over {max_age} days old asks for an update)
doctor_lists_stale: built {built}, {age} days old, over {max_age}: run  {launcher} lists update  (it goes online to fetch them) or upgrade {name}
doctor_path_none: not on PATH: run it as  {launcher}
doctor_path_other: {command} runs {path}, which is not this installation ({launcher}): run this one by its full path, or remove the other one
doctor_site_middleware: server-half middleware in the site's code
doctor_site_middleware_none: no file mounts {middleware}: setup --print --site says where it goes
doctor_site_middleware_beside: {files} missing beside the middleware's other files: copy it from {name}'s edge folder (setup --print --site)
doctor_site_middleware_static: not needed: a static site has no server code (the server half is optional)
doctor_site_middleware_unknown: not checked: the framework was not recognised
doctor_site_script_plugin: not in the files: the {name} plugin adds the line (a page opened with site_url shows it)
doctor_site_plugin_found: {files} (activate it under Plugins, and fill in Settings > {name})
doctor_site_plugin_none: the {name} plugin is not in wp-content/plugins: setup --print --site says how to add it
doctor_live_script_none: no cake.js line with this site key in the page
doctor_live_blocked: a sandbox (an AI tool's) blocks connections from here: run doctor in your own terminal, or allow network access
doctor_live_token_ok: Server-Timing cake, signed with this {name}'s secret, {age} s old
doctor_live_token_none: no cake entry in the response's Server-Timing: the middleware is not mounted, or the site's server has no {env}
doctor_live_token_bad: signed with another secret: the site's server needs this {name}'s, the value of  {launcher} secret print
doctor_live_token_stale: its time is {minutes} min away from this computer's clock, outside the window a token counts in: check both clocks
doctor_live_no_secret: this {name} has no secret yet, so it cannot read a token: run  {launcher} secret init  and give the site's server the value of  {launcher} secret print
doctor_live_token_optional: no token: this site has no server half (optional for a static site)
doctor_live_sec_fetch: token has the Sec-Fetch values doctor sent
doctor_live_signature: signature headers reach the site's server
doctor_live_lost: {headers} did not reach the site's server: something in front of it (a proxy, a CDN, a load balancer) removes them
doctor_live_not_checked: not checked: no token to read
doctor_live_no_url: not checked: save a page of the running site with  {launcher} config set site_url <address>  (or run doctor --url <address>)
setup_local: Local page:  {base}/        <- what the user opens; it is the whole product (dashboard, sessions, replay, settings)
If only 'visit received' fails: run  {launcher} ping  (one test visit, marked as a test), then doctor again.
If doctor says {name} is not running but '{command} start' fails with 'Operation not permitted', your sandbox blocks local
network access. Ask the user to run doctor in their own terminal or to allow network access; do not tell them to start {name} again.
Step 2. Tell the user, in their language:
- open {base}/ in their browser: first it asks them to register (theirs to do: never fill it in for them),
then it shows how to connect their website, step by step;
- visitors of a public website cannot reach 127.0.0.1 on this computer: for them, {name} runs on a server (SERVER.md);
- only if they ask you to connect the website: run  {launcher} setup --print --site  in the website's code folder.

setup_site_server_mode: Server mode:  public listener {listen}, path {prefix}: visitors' browsers reach {name} at {prefix}/ on the site's own domain (SERVER.md)
setup_site_settings: {launcher} config set site_domain <the site's domain, e.g. from a CNAME file or package.json homepage; ask the user if you cannot tell>

At the top of {file}, before any output:

setup_site_secret: The secret: run  {launcher} secret init  once (it says so when there is one already). The site's server reads it from
the environment variable {env}, set to what  {launcher} secret print  prints: for a dev server on this
computer, an env file the repository ignores (check .gitignore) or the command that starts it; on a live server, its
secret store. Never commit it. Without it the middleware does nothing.
setup_site_secret_wordpress: The secret: run  {launcher} secret init  once, then add  define( '{env}', '<what {launcher} secret print prints>' );
to wp-config.php above the line that says to stop editing (or set the environment variable {env}). Never commit it.
setup_site_check: Step 4. Check. Start the site the way it runs on this computer (its dev server, for example), save the address of one
of its pages, and run doctor:
{launcher} config set site_url <that page's address, e.g. http://localhost:3000/>
doctor reads the site's files, then opens that page the way a browser does: the page must load cake.js and, with the
server half, its response must carry {name}'s token with the Sec-Fetch values and signature headers doctor sent.
If the site cannot run here, say so and skip site_url: doctor then checks the files only.
If only a 'visit' line fails: open the site in a browser, or run  {launcher} ping  (one test visit), then doctor again.
setup_site_tell: Step 5. Tell the user: the local page URL, which files you changed, and what is left for them:
setup_site_tell_local: - a site running on this computer (dev server at localhost) sends visits to {name} right away;
- visitors of a public website cannot reach 127.0.0.1 on this computer: for them {name} has to run on a server the
website can reach (SERVER.md says how); deploying the site change is theirs;
setup_site_tell_server: - this {name} is in server mode: visitors' browsers reach it at {prefix}/ on the site's own domain, through the load
balancer's path rule (SERVER.md); deploying the site change, and giving the site's server the secret, is theirs;
setup_site_tell_privacy: - mention session recording in the site's privacy policy.
site_sentence: In this website's code folder, run `{launcher} setup --print --site`, follow the steps it prints to connect {name} to this website, then run `{launcher} doctor` and tell me the result and what is left for me to do.
web_not_built: {name}'s local pages are not built. In its web folder run  npm ci && npm run build  (the pages go to {folder}), or set CAKE_WEB_DIR to a folder that has them.
